judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The link "Managing Diabetes" is the title at the start of a bullet in a MedlinePlus resource list ("Start Here"). Each bullet reads: title link, NIH icon, then the source organization in parentheses, with "Also in Spanish" on a second line. On the live page the title is #006699, 14px, regular weight, with no underline at rest (underline only on hover). The visible text next to it is not the li's #444444, which is what the rule compared against. It is span.orgs/desc-text in #666666 at 12px. The color contrast is under 3:1 either way (about 1.1:1 against the gray annotation), but color is not the only cue. The link is the item's title, set larger (14px against 12px) and in its own position, ahead of a smaller parenthetical attribution. That is the "visually evident from page design and context" case F73 sets apart from links inside prose, much like the titles of a list of search results. The finding says "only by its color", but it checked underline, border, weight, style and icon and ignored the font-size difference and the list layout. That applies F73/G183's inline-text-link test more strictly than SC 1.4.1 requires. The trailing "Spanish" link (12px, same size as "Also in") would be a stronger 1.4.1 case, but it is not this finding. This is borderline, and a strict auditor might still flag it.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The header search submit button "GO" has white text, 14px bold. That is not large text (bold large text starts at 14pt, about 18.7px), so 4.5:1 applies. In the live page at rest, the background is a gradient (#329e39 to #2b8737 at 25% to #21662e), and the text, which runs from about 29% to 71% of the button height, sits on about #2b8737 or darker, roughly 4.5:1 or more. On hover the gradient changes to linear-gradient(#329e39 75%, #2b8737 100%), so the whole text sits on #329e39. White on #329e39 is 3.45:1, which I computed myself and which matches the probe. There is no text-shadow or other aid. Text in a state the user puts it in (hover) falls below 4.5:1, so this fails 1.4.3 as reported.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header search text input (#searchtext_primary). On keyboard focus (reached with 6 Tabs on the live page), the author style sets outline 0, changes the 1px border from #b4b4b4 to #66afe9 and adds a soft rgba(102,175,233,.6) glow. These pixels are indeed under 3:1 against white (the border is about 2.4:1 and the glow is lower), as the probe says. However, this is a text input: on focus it shows the text caret in caret-color #444444 (inherited from color), about 9.7:1 on the white field. The Understanding document for 1.4.11 (Figure 33, 'Text input focus style') rules this exact pattern a pass: a faint author outline (#CCC, 1.6:1) plus the visible caret, because the caret "does provide a sufficiently strong visual indication". Only a low-contrast custom caret fails (Figure 44), and that is not the case here. The probe measured only the ring and ignored the caret, so it applied a stricter test than 1.4.11 requires.
